state

The state property provides synchronous access to the current immutable state snapshot of a FeatureCell. This is the primary mechanism for reading state from a FeatureCell at a specific moment in time.

State Contract Summary

  • Returns the current state snapshot synchronously
  • Always reflects the latest committed state
  • Returns an immutable snapshot
  • Does not emit or subscribe to changes
  • Safe to read at any time after initialization

The state property exposes a read-only view of the FeatureCell’s most recent state snapshot. It does not participate in pipeline execution, does not trigger computation, and does not create subscriptions.

Note

The returned snapshot is immutable. Consumers must treat the snapshot as read-only and must not attempt to mutate its contents.

Example

The state property is typically used for synchronous reads, conditional logic, or imperative inspection where reactive subscription is not required.

Example: Reading FeatureCell State

{{`const snapshot = employeeCell.state;

console.info(snapshot.value);
console.info(snapshot.hasValue);
console.info(snapshot.isLoading);
console.info(snapshot.error);`}}

What this does

  • Reads the current FeatureCell state synchronously
  • Does not subscribe to future updates
  • Does not trigger pipeline execution
  • Returns a stable, immutable snapshot

This access pattern is ideal for imperative reads, guards, logging, debugging, or one-time inspection of state without reactive overhead.

Angular Integration

When /angular is installed, the state property is overridden with a signal-based state reference. Instead of returning a snapshot object, state exposes reactive Angular Signals for each state field.

This allows FeatureCell state to integrate directly with Angular’s reactivity model without subscriptions, async pipes, or manual change detection.

Angular State Surface

In Angular environments, state is a VaultSignalStateRef<T>:

  • Each state field is exposed as an Angular Signal
  • Signals update automatically when state changes
  • No subscriptions or teardown logic required
  • State remains immutable and read-only

Example: Reading FeatureCell State with Signals

{{`@Component({
  selector: 'employee-view',
  template: \`
    @if (state.hasValue()) {
      <div>
        <p>Employees: {{ state.value() | json }}</p>
      </div>
    }

    @if (state.isLoading()) {
      <div>
        Loading...
      </div>
    }

    @if (state.error()) {
      <div>
        Error: {{ state.error()?.message }}
      </div>
    }
  \`
})
export class EmployeeComponent {
  private bankEmployeeServce = inject(EmployeeService);
  state = this.bankEmployeeService.vault.state;
}`}}

What this does

  • Reads FeatureCell state reactively using Angular Signals
  • Automatically updates the view on state changes
  • Requires no subscriptions or manual cleanup
  • Preserves Vault immutability guarantees

This override is automatic when /angular is present. No configuration changes are required.
